caption:
HeyGen turns a script into a video of an AI avatar talking, either a stock presenter or a digital twin of you.
The free plan gives 1 to 3 short videos at 720p. Creator is $29 a month for 600 credits.
Here is how to make your first avatar video, clone yourself and keep the credit bill down.

slides.headline: How to use *HeyGen* to make an AI avatar video of yourself

slides.heading: 1. Start from a *script*
paras: Click Create Video, then Start from Scratch, and pick portrait or landscape.
Type your script scene by scene. HeyGen suggests under 2,000 characters per section.

slides.heading: 2. Clone *yourself*
paras: In Avatars, click New Avatar and choose Clone a real person. Record one take with no cuts.
Then read the consent text on camera. Without it the avatar cannot be used.

slides.heading: 3. Watch the *credits*
paras: Free gives 1 to 3 videos of up to a minute at 720p. Creator is $29 a month for 600 credits.
Avatar V costs 48 credits a minute, so 600 credits is about 12 minutes of video.

site_article.headline: How to use HeyGen to make an AI avatar video
site_article.dek: HeyGen turns a script into a video of a talking avatar, either a stock presenter or a digital twin of you. Here is the workflow, the consent step and what the credits really buy.
site_article.summary: HeyGen is an AI video tool that makes a talking avatar read your script, in AI Studio or from a single photo. The free plan covers 1 to 3 videos of up to one minute, and the Creator plan costs $29 a month for 600 credits.
site_article.seo_title: How to use HeyGen to make an AI avatar video
site_article.seo_description: How to use HeyGen: make your first avatar video in AI Studio, clone yourself with a digital twin, pass the consent check and see what free and $29 plans give.
site_article.answer_summary: Click Create Video, choose Start from Scratch, pick an avatar and a voice, type your script and click Generate. To use your own face, create a digital twin under Avatars with New Avatar and Clone a real person, then record the consent video.
site_article.hero_alt: A creator records footage of themselves with a phone and a ring light, with a progress panel beside them.

paragraphs.text: HeyGen makes videos of an AI avatar reading a script you type. You can use one of its stock avatars, animate a photo, or build a digital twin from a short video of yourself. According to HeyGen's help center, the Free plan includes 1 to 3 free videos depending on your region, each up to one minute long and shared as a 720p link, plus 500+ stock avatars and one custom video avatar.

The fastest way to learn it is to make one short video with a stock avatar first, then decide whether a digital twin of you is worth the effort. This guide follows that order and ends with the part most people get wrong: credits.
Make your first avatar video in AI Studio

paragraphs.title: 1. Start a new project
paragraphs.text: Log in, click Create Video and select Start from Scratch. Choose portrait or landscape. You can change the orientation later, so pick the one that fits where the video will go: portrait for Reels and TikTok, landscape for YouTube and slides.

paragraphs.title: 2. Pick an avatar
paragraphs.text: AI Studio opens with a default avatar on the canvas. Click Avatars above the canvas to choose another one. Click the avatar on the canvas to change its look, framing, background and animations.

paragraphs.title: 3. Choose a voice
paragraphs.text: In the voice settings you can change accent, tone, speed, voice model and voice engine. Press Play next to the voice to hear your script read aloud. Once all your scenes are written, go back and click Apply to all scenes so the whole video uses the same voice.

paragraphs.title: 4. Write the script, scene by scene
paragraphs.text: A scene is a block of script plus the avatar and anything else on screen. Type your script in the text field. HeyGen recommends keeping each section under 2,000 characters. Click + Scene to add a blank scene or one from a template, and put the cursor where you want a breath and click Pause to add one. Pauses grow or shrink in half second steps.

You cannot watch a full preview of the avatar while you edit. You can listen to the script as audio, but the lip sync only appears in the rendered video. Render a 20 second test before you write a ten minute script.

paragraphs.title: 5. Generate the video
paragraphs.text: Click Generate, name the video, pick a folder and choose the output resolution. The finished video appears in the Projects tab when processing ends. If HeyGen warns No Avatar in Video, the final file will have no speaking avatar, so check the avatar before you submit.
Make a digital twin of yourself

A digital twin is an avatar built from video of a real person. HeyGen's help center says even a Free account gets one digital twin slot. Its Avatar V model, according to the company, can build a likeness from a single 15 second phone recording.

paragraphs.title: 6. Record your training footage
paragraphs.text: Go to Avatar, then Avatars, click New Avatar and choose Clone a real person. You can record with your webcam, record on your phone by scanning a QR code, or upload footage in MP4, MOV, WebM or WebP up to 10GB. Then click Create Avatar.

The footage decides how good the twin looks. HeyGen's guidelines ask for one continuous take with no cuts, at least 1080p at 30fps, bright even light, a simple static background and a quiet room. Look into the lens, keep your hands from covering your face and avoid big logos, text on clothing and large accessories. The help article asks for at least two minutes of footage for best results, even though the recording screen promises 15 seconds.

paragraphs.title: 7. Record the consent video
paragraphs.text: HeyGen will not let you make videos with a twin until it verifies consent. The person in the avatar records a clip under 30 seconds reading the consent text exactly as shown, including any code. It must be the same person as in the footage. You can build a twin of someone else, but they have to record their own consent clip, for example from their phone through the QR code.

If the check fails, the avatar is rejected and the reason shows on its card on the Avatars page. HeyGen lists a different person on camera, a recording of a screen, and dark, blurry or muffled video as common causes. Training usually takes 10 to 20 minutes for footage that is not 4K, according to the help center.

paragraphs.title: 8. Or animate a photo instead
paragraphs.text: If you do not want to film yourself, create a Photo Avatar under Avatars, hover over it and select Quick Create. That opens Single Scene. In Presenter Mode you add a script or audio, pick a voice and an avatar engine, choose landscape or portrait and click Generate. An optional Custom Motion prompt describes gestures.

paragraphs.title: Custom Motion prompt to try
paragraphs.text: Speaks calmly to the camera, nods once at the start, and uses small open hand gestures at chest height. Keeps both hands below the chin.
What HeyGen costs in practice

Paid plans run on credits. HeyGen's pricing article lists Creator at $29 a month with 600 credits, 1080p export, watermark removal and videos up to 30 minutes. Pro starts at $49 a month for 1,000 credits and exports in 4K. Business is $149 a month for the first seat. Unused credits on monthly plans carry over for one more billing cycle, and they are lost if you cancel down to Free.

The model you pick changes the bill. Avatar III Video Look costs 4 credits a minute, Avatar IV Video Look 31 and Avatar V 48 credits a minute. Video Agent, which builds a whole video from a text prompt, costs 80 credits a minute in standard mode. At 48 credits a minute, the 600 Creator credits cover about 12 minutes of Avatar V video.
What HeyGen is bad at

HeyGen holds a 4.7 rating from 322 reviews on Capterra, where users praise the easy interface and realistic avatars. The most common complaint is price: credits run out fast and custom avatars cost extra. Reviewers also report hands that distort, avatars that change look between scenes, mispronounced words, slow renders for long videos, and lost credits or videos after downgrading.

HeyGen is good at one job: a person talking to the camera, in many languages, without filming every time. It is weaker the moment you need hands, movement or long scenes. Start on the free plan with a stock avatar, test a 30 second script on the model you plan to use, and only pay once you know how many minutes a month you really make.
